text.p: Asia Equity brokerage recommended a sell on Indonesian tobacco company PT Hanjaya Mandala Sampoerna on Tuesday, saying it had revised down its forecast for the firm's 1997 net profit by 9.5 percent to 451 billion rupiah.
"Weak sales data in the first part of the year plus scant opportunities for price rises going forward point to the share price disappointing in the medium-term," the brokerage said in a report.
Sampoerna was down 50 rupiah at 9,175 in afternoon trade.
"Stick sales figures for 1997 are likely to disappoint, and price rises are not on the cards," Asia Equity said.

The brokerage said Sampoerna had incurred significant debt because of capacity expansion in 1996 and that interest expenses were likely to mount to 143 billion rupiah in 1998 from 22 billion rupiah in 1995.
"In the long-term, the company remains fairly attractive as capacity increases should exceed production well into 2000 and non-manufacturing endeavours should begin to pay off," Asia Equity said.
"However, the short-term difficulties warrant keeping the counter under observation from the sidelines in the next few months."
